- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0x recent mean), model often overshoots; apply decay factor (e.g., 0.8–0.9) to subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 15–25% for 1–3d horizon.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast > 2.5x recent mean, reduce by 20–40% for 7–30d horizon.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven tail risks; add 5–15% buffer if sentiment volatility > 0.4 over last 5d.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 10–20% for 1–5d horizon.
